# Recorded PTY frames

Each `*.json` here is a verbatim recording of what a CLI actually wrote to a
pty, chunk by chunk, with a `t` in milliseconds since spawn and the raw bytes
base64-encoded. They exist because the first-run boot bugs in ticket
`K1e5pkaG26GhUaKSrMcV` were invisible to reasoning: the code's assumptions about
these screens read fine, and the real bytes disagreed.

Two things you only learn from real frames:

- **Claude paints with cursor moves, not spaces.** `⏵⏵ bypass permissions on`
  arrives as `⏵⏵\x1b[6Gbypass\x1b[13Gpermissions\x1b[25Gon`, so after ANSI
  stripping it reads `bypasspermissionson`. Any marker written with literal
  spaces matches one render path and misses another. Write markers with `\s*`,
  or key off a glyph.
- **Codex paints a composer before it has one.** `? for shortcuts` and
  `Ask Codex` show up at ~120 ms on a skeleton whose header still says
  `model: loading`, ~200 ms _before_ the login or trust dialog replaces it.

## Re-capturing

Nothing here is generated by the test suite; regenerate by hand when a CLI
changes shape. Isolate the CLI's config so you never touch your own:

```sh
# claude — first run, stopping at the bypass-permissions consent screen
mkdir -p /tmp/mb-home /tmp/mb-proj
echo '{"hasCompletedOnboarding":true,"theme":"dark"}' > /tmp/mb-home/.claude.json
cd /tmp/mb-proj && HOME=/tmp/mb-home claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
#   → "Do you trust this folder?"      → Enter
#   → "2. Yes, I accept"               ← the screen these fixtures capture
# To reach it again on later runs, delete `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`
# from /tmp/mb-home/.claude/settings.json — that, NOT .claude.json, is where
# Claude Code 2.1.238 records the acceptance.

# codex — first run, stopping at the ChatGPT login menu
mkdir -p /tmp/mb-codex
cd /tmp/mb-proj && CODEX_HOME=/tmp/mb-codex codex \
  -c 'approval_policy="never"' -c 'sandbox_mode="danger-full-access"'
```

Drive that through `node-pty` and append one record per `onData` chunk:
`{ "t": <ms since spawn>, "b64": <base64 of the raw chunk> }`. Keep the `note`
field saying which CLI version and which machine state produced it — a fixture
with no provenance is worse than no fixture.
